---
title: "Text: what the play-by-play says about each player"
---

```{python}
#| label: takeaways
import pandas as pd
from _viz import read, md
r = read("step4_text_vs_archetypes.csv")
zs = r[(r.league == "both") & (r.method == "zero-shot from written descriptions")].iloc[0]
hz = r[r.method.str.startswith("zero-shot") & r.method.str.contains("hand")].accuracy_vs_hand_labels.iloc[0]
hs = r[r.method.str.startswith("stat archetype")].accuracy_vs_hand_labels.iloc[0]
tc = r[r.method.str.startswith("text clustering")].set_index("league")
md(f"""::: {{.callout-note appearance="simple"}}
## Takeaways
- **Every play already has a written description**, e.g. "Pullup Jump Shot", "Cutting Dunk Shot", "(X assists)",
  "X blocks Y's shot". Treating each player-season's plays as a document gives a text layer with no scraping.
- **Topics found from text alone match recognizable roles:** rim finishers, post scorers, pull-up shooters and
  spot-up shooters.
- **Text groups partly agree with the stat archetypes** (ARI {tc.loc['NBA', 'ari_vs_stat_archetype']:.2f} NBA,
  {tc.loc['WNBA', 'ari_vs_stat_archetype']:.2f} WNBA). The text sees *how* players score and pass; the stat model also sees
  usage, rebounding rates and defense.
- **Zero-shot labels** (from written role descriptions, checked against the player's position) agree with the stat
  archetypes {zs.accuracy_vs_stat_archetype:.0%} of the time (chance is about 17%), and with the blind hand labels
  {hz:.0%} of the time, close to the stat archetypes' {hs:.0%}.
:::""")
```

## How it works

- **Documents:** one per player-season (NBA 2017-18 onward and WNBA 2019 onward, where the play text names shot
  types; at least 500 minutes).
- **Tokens:**
  - **Shot type** (e.g. *pullup jump shot three*). A made shot and a missed shot of the same type are the **same
    token**, weighted: each attempt counts once and each make counts again. A movement shooter who takes and makes
    many threes scores high on *jump shot three*; a defender who takes them and misses still shows the shot, with less weight.
  - **Playmaking:** each assist records what the pass set up: *assist to a three*, *to the rim* or *to the mid-range*.
  - **Defense and possession:** blocks, steals, rebounds, and all turnover types merged into one *turnover* token.
- **Preprocessing:** lower-casing, punctuation stripped, one token per play type, administrative events (substitutions,
  timeouts) removed, play types used by fewer than 20 players dropped.
- **TF-IDF:** term frequency (dampened) times inverse document frequency, so a rare play like an *alley-oop dunk* weighs
  more than a common *defensive rebound*.
- **Position cross-check:** the distinctive plays of each archetype are measured against players **at the same
  listed position**; text clustering uses the text plus the player's position; a zero-shot label must fit the position
  (a center can't be labeled a secondary guard).
- **Embeddings:** LSA, a 50-dimension compression of TF-IDF that places related play types together (no download needed).
- **Topic model:** non-negative matrix factorization, 8 topics. **Text clustering:** K-Means (k = 6).
- **Zero-shot labeling:** each archetype was described in words before results were seen; each player gets the most
  similar description that fits their position. The hand labels were only used to score the result.

## Plays that set each archetype apart

The plays most over-represented in each archetype compared with players **at the same position**, split into shots and
playmaking & defense, so common but defining actions like passing aren't crowded out by rare shot types.

```{python}
a = read("step4_archetype_tokens.csv")
a["token"] = a.token.str.replace("__", " ", regex=False).str.replace("_", " ", regex=False)
for lg in ["NBA", "WNBA"]:
    t = a[a.league == lg].groupby(["archetype", "category"]).token.agg(", ".join).unstack().reindex(columns=["shots", "playmaking & defense"])
    md(f"**{lg}**\n\n" + t.fillna("(nothing above same-position players)").reset_index().to_markdown(index=False))
md("**What this shows:** creators and secondary guards stand out for pull-ups, step-backs and assists of every kind; "
   "spot-up 3-and-D wings for catch-and-shoot threes, steals and rebounds; rim-running bigs for dunks, putbacks and "
   "blocks. One finding to note: **hub bigs / point forwards do not pass more than other forwards and centers** in this "
   "data. The group is defined more by post scoring (turnaround hooks and fades) than by playmaking, so its true "
   "point-forward passers (Jokić-type players) are better identified by their sub-type and assist rates than by the group name.")
```

```{python}
t = read("step4_topics.csv")

```

## How well text matches the stat archetypes

ARI and NMI: 0 = no agreement, 1 = identical groupings.

```{python}
r2 = r.rename(columns={"ari_vs_stat_archetype": "ARI", "nmi_vs_stat_archetype": "NMI",
                       "accuracy_vs_stat_archetype": "accuracy vs stat archetype",
                       "accuracy_vs_hand_labels": "accuracy vs hand labels"})
md(r2.round(3).fillna("").to_markdown(index=False))
```

Text clusters (rows, named by their three most distinctive play types) against stat archetypes (columns), both leagues:

```{python}
c = read("step4_text_cluster_vs_archetype.csv").set_index("text_cluster_name")
c.index = c.index.str.replace("__", " ", regex=False).str.replace("_", " ", regex=False)
md(c.to_markdown())
md("**What this shows:** each row is a group the text found on its own; the numbers are how many player-seasons of each "
   "stat archetype landed in it. Rows dominated by one column (e.g. the pull-up row by creators and secondary guards) "
   "mean the text and the stats agree; spread-out rows are roles the text alone can't separate.")
```

## Reputation text (next step)

How teams are *described* (offense-first, defense-first) can be compared with how they *played*. The program
`scripts/fetch_team_text.py` downloads team-season articles from Wikipedia's official API (rate-limited, cached
locally, not republished), and `src/step4_reputation.py` scores offense/defense emphasis and sentiment with TF-IDF
and word lists, then compares them with measured team identity. It has to run on a computer that can reach Wikipedia.
